title: Mass-Action Law-Median Principle Algorithm for Biodynamics and Informatics Reveals Equivalence or Analogy to Major Historical Mathematical and Physical Theories
content: The Mass Action Law (MAL) Median-Effect equation, fa/fu = (D/Dm)^m, leads to the Unified General Dynamics Theory and algorithm, which provide interdisciplinary and cross-disciplinary common linkage parameters for computerized, digital, efficient, cost-effective, Econo-green scientific R&D and data science informatics. The MAL is a general theory for drug and entity dynamics actions with common parameters (Dm and m), and dose-effect interaction in combinations with a unified combination index equation (CIE), which allows digital simulation of synergism (CI < 1), additive effect (CI =1), and antagonism (CI > 1). Chou - Talalay’s isobologram, represented by a right triangle (a1 + b1 = c1), is dimensionally corresponding to the Pythagorean theorem (a2 + b2 = c2) and Fermat’s Last Theorem (an + bn = cn), which has no positive integer solution for any integer n greater than 2. The MAL-based input-output sequence, pattern transition, and combinatorics of enzyme reactions led to the discovery of the Second Degree (Squared) Pascal triangle. Surprisingly, life-science dynamics can be linked to Riemann’s zeta hypothesis, ζ(s) at s = 2, the critical line of prime distribution, the critical strip (0–1), and Euler’s Prime Product Function and its properties. The universe has two domains: Life and Non-Life, which manifest the dimensionless relativity ratio with basic codes. For life, a/b = a/(1-a) = (1-b)/b (Floating Ratio), and for non-life, a/b = (a + b)/a = 1 + b/a, or (Golden Ratio). Life and Non-Life can be linked by the two fractional finite and continuous distribution functions of “1”. Life is finite, discrete, and binary, cyclable with the Median-based equilibrium, symmetry, harmony, homeostasis, and optimal conditions; Non-Life is open, fractal, and extendable to infinity, as in mathematics, physics, and AI. Despite numerous mathematical equations derived and established since antiquity, fundamental principles in biomedical science constitute only a small fraction of them. Human existence constitutes a tiny fraction of the universe. However, humans evolve and decide the units and methods of measurement in all branches of science. This paper presents a unified MAL median-based, top-down R&D approach, distinct from traditional, statistics-based, bottom-up R&D. MAL input-output dynamics enable deterministic digital informatics through computer simulations and automation, with efficient, cost-effective features not accessible in traditional, specific-aimed, consensus-based, regulated R&D.
